cells.tense: You are here with it, adjusting what needs adjusting as you go.
cells.ask: Point at one thing you keep steady and name, to yourself or someone, the direction you'll turn it toward next.
cells.core:
You read the room and yourself at the same time, and the corrections are small enough that nobody notices them. That's the work — adding a little here, easing off there, keeping the whole thing moving without a jolt. Something that started vague has a real weight now, and you're still carrying it. The proof isn't in a story you tell about it; it's that it's still moving and you're the one adjusting.

The next thing you feed is a sense of where this points. Not a five-year plan — just the bearing you'd set if things got rough. You don't have to know the whole road. You just have to want something specific enough to aim at, and then aim it.
cells.sheetLine: You keep it moving by adjusting, and you know where it's headed.
cells.place: In the ongoing adjustment that keeps things flowing

cells.tense: You are bracing for a future you can already feel going wrong.
cells.ask: Step back from one decision you've been forcing and let the next move come from what you actually see now, not what you dread.
cells.core:
You've got your hands too tight on the wheel. Everything that started as a possibility has become a load you're defending, so every adjustment feels like it has to be perfect or the whole thing tips. You're not tuning anymore — you're gripping. The future you're bracing for is a story you wrote, and you're spending the present inside it while nothing here gets your eyes.

The way back is to see what's actually here before deciding what to do about it. Not plan, not brace — just look. One thing at a time, without the weight of what you think it means. The load can hold itself a minute while you get your sight back and let the next step come from what's actually in front of you.
cells.sheetLine: You're gripping the wheel and driving into a future that hasn't happened.
cells.place: In the ongoing adjustment that keeps things flowing

cells.tense: You are still standing at a threshold you already walked through.
cells.ask: Let one person or one situation show you something different from what you've settled on, and stay with what arrives instead of turning away.
cells.core:
You built something real and then stopped showing up for it. When it's alive, you're in the middle of it — noticing what's off, making the small corrections, staying close enough to feel the thing move under your hands. That's what tuning is. Right now you've stepped back from it and gone quiet, so the adjusting has stopped, not because the work ended but because you left the room.

What's called for isn't effort. It's the willingness to let something reach you again. Let one person or one situation in without needing to know how it ends. You're not outside anything you made. You're just not letting it touch you, and that part can move today.
cells.sheetLine: You stopped showing up for what you built and call it done.
cells.place: In the ongoing adjustment that keeps things flowing

cells.tense: You are already steering this, though you talk as if it steers itself.
cells.ask: Say 'I decided this' about the timing or the situation you've been calling outside you, and notice what shifts when you own it.
cells.core:
You're making the calls — what gets added, what gets cut, how things blend — but you describe it like it just happened to you. The work is moving through your hands, and you're calling it how things are. When it's healthy, you can see the line between what you aimed at and what's here now, and saying that out loud doesn't frighten you. Right now that line is invisible, so the load feels like it arrived from somewhere and sat down.

The move isn't more effort. It's seeing the link between what you meant and what's in front of you. Naming your hand in it doesn't change the load. It changes who's holding it.
cells.sheetLine: You're steering this already, and the hand on it is yours.
cells.place: In the ongoing adjustment that keeps things flowing
